Joined by the term Pricing, a reading: BigCommerce's Pricing API, 'Get product pricing on BigCommerce-hosted storefronts' (BC-S-0053), the price of a product, which Salla's webhook product.price.updated names (SA-S-1599) and WooCommerce's Marketplace category Pricing names without saying what it holds (WC-S-0735). Strained: no platform defines CM-CAT-013, and what its other cells show is setting a product's price (Salla's Automatic pricing, Zid's Custom Product Pricing) or apps for it; BigCommerce's Pricing API reads prices for a storefront, with no scopes, through CORS (BC-S-0054). Whether reading a storefront's prices and setting them are one capability isn't stated. The API group is a place of its own (BC-I-0049), so a reviewer may split it into a capability. Price lists, which set prices for customer groups, are BC-C-007, domain D.

Salla's import and export: its Import & export and Import customers links, the Merchant API folder Exports and the exports scope, the import_export_management permission, plan lines and flags (SA-S-1805, SA-S-1847, SA-S-1057, SA-S-2257). It is coarser than the capabilities, so it lands in the parent; its Advanced import and Export templates statements are cited in CM-MIG-002 and CM-MIG-003, in this tree. Strained: its Export log link (SA-S-1890) is cited in CM-MIG-004, which Salla's route puts under its logs, another tree. Q1's M-083 holds it with WooCommerce's product import and export (WC-C-067), which WooCommerce's part lands; the match holds no Shopify concern (its note: Shopify's export permissions sit in its products, orders and customers concerns), so the join here is single.

Salla's status page (SA-S-0047) is the concern's statement of this capability. Strained: its plan line for platform stability (SA-I-1197) is cited in CM-OPS-001, another tree; its API security statements (HTTPS only, SA-S-0175; TLS, SA-S-0174; OAuth, SA-S-0176; the Security Considerations doc, SA-S-1006) are the API's conventions, domain F's by scope.tsv's rule, and its mandatory two-step verification (SA-S-5115) is sign-in security, domain A's (U-006, apart). None of these is cited in G. Most of the concern is security, and scope.tsv names A under also, not F.

Salla's statements of what happens when a partner fails: its exemption from liability for technical faults and payment-gateway updates in affiliate commissions (SA-S-0044), its assigning an order to the next shipping company when the first doesn't deliver to the customer's area (SA-S-0162), and its telling the store that a communication failed (SA-S-0194). No platform gives partner failures a place of its own (convention 2), so the concern lands in the reliability capability, not one of its own. Strained: each statement is about one kind of partner, whose subject is another domain's (shipping companies, C; communication apps, F; the affiliate program's commissions), and Q1's gaps hold no statement of where or how Salla handles an unavailable gateway or carrier (where, decides and reason: page not read).

Salla's store migration service under its own terms on partners.salla.com (SA-S-5119): the platform, owned by شركة منصة سلة للاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات, provides a service to ease moving from other e-commerce platforms (SA-S-5121, SA-S-5123), with its eligibility (SA-S-5120) and the carrying over of the previous platform's balance (SA-S-5122). Single: no Shopify concern lands here; Shopify's side of U-081 (SH-C-020's Store data importer apps) is domain B's and is cited in CM-MIG-001.
